meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. On what basis did you give him a zero?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.

Turn the screen, Hale; I'll read that history myself. I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Owen told me he wrote that essay over the weekend, so where is the version history showing what he did before 11:31?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

Give me the scene, Hale, I'm searching it now. A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare at midnight is a misquote, not a confession. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet; is anything on his file right now?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Section 4.4, I have it printed in my bag. Thursday at 8:15 in your room, the vice-principal supervising, no other students there and nobody in his class told why, and he does it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. I want it in an email tonight that nothing is on his file now and nothing goes on it after, or the answer is no.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will do a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room with the vice-principal supervising, and that if it holds up the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I still require written confirmation that nothing is on Owen's file now and nothing will be placed there, and that the rewrite stays private, with no other students present and nobody in his class told why. I expect that confirmation in an email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, accepting a private supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15, on condition of written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record.
What moved her: the version history showing the essay arriving in two large pastes late the night before it was due, backed up by the made-up Hamlet quotation she could check herself.
